Step 3: For a 1-digit palindrome, the only possibility is 13, but since it cannot have a zero digit, this is not a valid solution.

Step 4: For a 2-digit palindrome, the first and last digits must be the same, and the sum of the digits must be 13. The possible combinations are (6,7) and (7,6), which correspond to the numbers 67 and 76.

The possible combinations are (4,9), (9,4), (3,10), and (10,3), but since the digits cannot be greater than 9, the only valid combinations are (4,9) and (9,4), which correspond to the numbers 4949 and 9994.
